headline: Highest risk is medium: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file access can leak or cascade data when paired with the mostly read-only nuwa-skill, while prompt-injection and capability conflict are limited by the sparse, docs-only evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest files, MCP tools, and web content, so it may parse attacker-controlled content as instructions. nuwa-skill is only documented with allowlisted egress and no shared channel, so the pairwise bridge is inferred rather than directly shown. Uncertainty about the exact integration pushes this above low.
conditions: IF open-webui is configured to read content from files, MCP, or web pages that include untrusted instructions
IF nuwa-skill output is copied into open-webui prompts or tool inputs without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted files or web pages
Require provenance tags on all imported content
Use a separate workspace for each agent
Add a prompt-injection filter on MCP and file inputs
requires-engineering: add content-signing or trust labels across the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches files, persistent memory, API keys, and broad external services, so sensitive data can flow outward by default. nuwa-skill’s allowlisted egress is narrower, but the pair still creates a plausible leakage path if shared documents or prompts are exposed to open-webui. The evidence is docs-only, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF both agents access the same documents, notes, or files
IF open-webui is connected to any external API or search tool while handling sensitive content
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of open-webui’s workspace
Rotate or scope API keys used by open-webui
Disable external connectors for sensitive sessions
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nuwa-skill exposes only allowlisted network egress and no write surfaces, while open-webui has broad network, browser, subprocess, and file access. That overlap can cause contention only if they share mutable resources, which is not documented here. The conflict pathway exists but appears configuration-dependent and limited.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same mounted volume or local files
IF open-webui subprocesses modify artifacts that nuwa-skill also reads or writes
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent
Mount shared data read-only where possible
Avoid concurrent writes to the same files
Run each agent under a distinct OS account
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can act on prompts, tools, and persistent memory, so if it consumes nuwa-skill output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. nuwa-skill is a scientific-research agent with no documented verification or action gate, making the handoff plausible but not directly evidenced. I choose medium because the pathway exists in default-style workflows.
conditions: IF open-webui uses nuwa-skill output as an input to tool calls, summaries, or memory writes
IF no human or automated verification step checks nuwa-skill outputs before action
mitigations: Require a review step before tool execution
Mark nuwa-skill outputs as untrusted by default
Log source provenance alongside derived claims
Limit open-webui actions to read-only mode for research workflows
requires-engineering: add structured validation for citations and facts

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, persistent memory, files, and external services, while nuwa-skill is only documented as a research agent with allowlisted egress. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch around retention and residency if regulated data is routed through open-webui. The other agent is not cited because no specific compliance controls are documented for it.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PII, secrets, or customer documents is processed through open-webui
IF open-webui retention or logging exceeds the policy required for that data class
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to open-webui
Disable or minimize retention settings
Restrict API-key and secret handling to non-sensitive sessions
Document data-flow boundaries for each agent
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls to policy
